m: Bayburt Province (Turkish: Bayburt ili) is a province of Turkey. Located in the Northeast Anatolia region of the country, the capital city is Bayburt. Its area is 3,746 km2, and its population is 84,241 (2022), making it the least-populous province in Turkey. The province was created in 1989 from part of Gümüşhane Province.

e-sirakayalar-selalesi: A waterfall pouring down a rocky slope in Bayburt. With the green area around it, it is a favorite summer spot for picnics and photos.
Q4849566: Baksı Museum is a museum located in Bayburt, Turkey. “Baksı” literally means “healer, helper, protector” in Turkic languages. The museum offers contemporary art and traditional handcrafts. The basic aim of the foundation is, as quoted by founder Professor Hüsamettin Koçan, to "disseminate art and culture by bringing together contemporary and traditional art, to collect, document, classify, preserve and promote works of contemporary and traditional art, to use this base in realizing creation, and to hand local and national cultural values down to future generations".
Q6042116: Bayburt Castle (Turkish: Bayburt Kalesi) is a historic castle on a hill overlooking Bayburt, Turkey.
Q7916263: Varzahan, was an Armenian church founded in the 12th century near village Uğrak (formerly Varzahan), 10 km northwest of Bayburt, in eastern Turkey. After the Armenian genocide in 1915, it was demolished sometime between the 1920s and the mid-1950s.
Q56280876: Mount Kop Defense National Historic Park

Mount Kop Defense National Historic Park (Turkish: Kop Dağı Müdafaası Tarihî Millî Parkı) is a protected national historic site located between the provinces Bayburt and Erzurum in eastern Turkey dedicated to the events during the defense of Mount Kop against the Imperial Russian Army in the World War I. It was established in 2016.

Q61072521: Bayburt Grand Mosque is a Friday mosque in Bayburt. It is believed to date from the reign of the Anatolian Seljuk sultan Mesud II (1282–1298) and was rebuilt in the 1970s true to its original plan.
Q118955949: The Kenan Yavuz Ethnography Museum is in the village of Beşpınar, formerly Loru, in the Demirözü district of Bayburt.
Q21524214: Bayburt Clock Tower stands in the central district of Bayburt. Its clocks first ran on 29 October 1924. It was inspired by clock towers that Bayburt's soldiers had seen while fighting elsewhere during the War of Independence, and its style resembles Çorum Clock Tower. On a round base, the shaft is octagonal and the top square.
Q28219863: The Aydıntepe underground City (Turkish: Aydıntepe Yeraltı Şehri) is an ancient underground city in Aydıntepe district of Bayburt Province, Turkey. It is located 25 km (16 mi) northwest of Bayburt beneath a residential area.
Q6092334: Büyüktepe Höyük is a settlement mound 35 km southwest of Bayburt, 5 km north of Demirözü and 1 km north of Çiftetaş village, and is seen as the most important mound in the area. It is made of two hills joined by a saddle, in the well-watered Beşpınar Valley.
